title: Cost allocation: journey map, invoice export schema, and grooming notes
content:
Purpose
: capture a working UX + backlog for getting reliable CSV/JSON invoice exports and UI flows for cost allocation rules. Focus: export schema, journey map for finance users, alerts interplay, and prioritization for near-term sprint.

Context / problem statement
- Finance and platform teams need a single exportable invoice that includes per-cost-center allocation so they can ingest into Netsuite / internal ERPs.
- Today exports are token-level + aggregated but lack allocation breakdowns and metadata (currency, tax/vat, invoice status, allocation rule id).
- We need: 1) clear UI to define allocation rules (percent / usage-based / custom charge), 2) consistent export schema (CSV + JSONL), 3) scheduling and delivery (download, email, SFTP), 4) alerts when export generation fails or allocations mismatch thresholds.

Audience
- Primary: Finance Ops, Revenue Ops, Internal Platform teams at customers (power users).
- Secondary: Engineering (backend export service), Support (triage failed exports), Sales (enterprise deals referencing export capabilities).

Wireframe / journey notes (high level)
1) Billing home -> tabbed nav: Invoices | Allocations | Exports | Alerts
2) Allocations list: rows show allocation name, type (percent / rule), last run, mapped cost centers, linked invoices count, status
3) Allocation editor (modal or route):
   - Name, scope (org / project / model), rule type: fixed-percentage | usage-proportional | hybrid | custom mapping table
   - Preview pane: sample invoice preview for last closed invoice (toggle show raw vs allocated view)
   - Test button: run on sample period (async) and surface top-3 surprising reallocations
4) Invoice view: header with invoice metadata (id, period, total_usd, currency, tax_breakdown, invoice_status), tabs for "Summary" (aggregates) and "Allocations" (table rows per cost center).
5) Export flow: Export modal -> choose format (CSV/JSONL), time window, include allocation details toggle, delivery method (download / email / SFTP / API callback). Schedule option: one-off or recurring (monthly/quarterly/custom cron). Add retention policy.

Export schema - CSV sample (must map to API fields)
Header suggestion:
invoice_id,customer_id,period_start,period_end,generated_at,currency,total_amount_usd,sub_total_usd,tax_amount_usd,invoice_status,cost_center,allocation_rule_id,allocation_type,allocation_value,allocation_percentage,allocated_amount_usd,notes,source_model,token_count,raw_cost_usd
Sample row example:
inv_2025_02_001,acct_9876,2025-02-01,2025-02-28,2025-03-01T03:12:00Z,USD,12500.00,12000.00,500.00,final,cc-sales,rule_pct_23,percent,project-wide,30,3750.00,"includes surcharge for premium models",gpt-4-x,450000,12000.00
Notes on schema:
- allocated_amount_usd must sum to total_amount_usd across cost_centers or we mark exported_as_reconciled=false
- include both raw_cost_usd (system cost before allocation) and allocated_amount_usd (post-allocation)
- include allocation_rule_id so downstream systems can reconcile changes in rules over time
- if VAT/tax applied per-region, we include tax_region_code and tax_breakdown_json when exporting JSONL

JSONL variant
- one JSON per invoice with nested arrays for allocations (for systems that accept JSON). We'll export JSONL for API consumers; CSV for legacy ERPs.

Acceptance criteria (for MVP export)
- UI: allocation editor can create percent and usage-proportional rules and show preview within UI
- Export: user can generate a CSV that includes allocation lines and matches the header spec above
- Delivery: one-off download + schedule to email works; SFTP in scope as enterprise gated feature
- Checks: exported allocations either reconcile or export flags show mismatch; failures generate alert in Alerts panel and send email to admins

Backlog / prioritization (rough)
P0 (sprint 1):
- Allocation editor (percent + usage-proportional) + preview (UI + minimal backend) — estimate: 5 dev days + 2 QA
- CSV export generation endpoint + UI download modal — estimate: 4 dev days + 1 QA
- Alerts for export failure + retry UI — estimate: 2 dev days
P1 (next):
- Recurring schedule + email delivery (SES template + tenant settings) — 6 dev days
- Include tax_region and VAT breakdown in JSON exports — 3 dev days
- Test harness: sample invoice run button + UX for showing diffs — 3 dev days
P2 (later):
- SFTP delivery + large file streaming + pagination for CSVs — 8 dev days
- Custom mapping UI for column names / ERP templates — 5 dev days
- CSV schema versioning and migration path — 4 dev days

Edge cases / open questions
- Currency rounding: do we allocate on raw cost_usd and then round per-cost-center, or round on the allocated_amount_usd? (impact on reconciliation)
- Rewrites of allocation rules after invoice generation: should we allow retroactive reallocation? If yes, mark invoice as "reallocated_vX" and create audit trail. Need legal/finance signoff.
- Exports for very large invoices (millions of lines for token-level breakdown) — implement sampling vs full export. Consider compressing CSV, streaming S3 expiring link.
- How to represent credits/discounts: pro-rated across cost-centers or attached to payer only? Default: pro-rate by allocation weights, but allow override in allocation rule.

Design constraints and non-functional requirements
- Export generation must be idempotent and retry-safe (no duplicates on retry)
- Exports must not include PII (mask user ids) unless tenant explicitly requested and signed off
- GDPR: if tenant requests data deletion, ensure export history can be flushed per retention policy
- Performance: generation for mid-sized org (<100k lines) should complete within 2 minutes; larger exports use async streaming job with job id

Support/operational runbook notes (for SRE/support)
- Job naming scheme: export:tenant:<yyyy-mm>:<invoice_id>:<format>
- Logs to include allocation_rule_id and job_trace_id for debugging
- Failure reasons: SFTP timeout, transform error (bad chars), overflow memory. For each, surface friendly message + link to support runbook

Mockups / sketch notes (quick)
- Allocation editor: left pane form, right pane preview -> show reallocations with small colored bars representing percent allocations
- Invoice exports page: table with filter (period/customer/cost_center), bulk actions (download selected invoices), scheduled exports list with last_run status

Open UX decisions to land
- Single page vs modal for allocation editor (modal is faster to ship, single page better for complex mapping) -> prefer modal for MVP
- Default export format: CSV for new users, but UI should remember last used format per user
- Should "include allocation details" default to on for tenants with >1 cost_center? propose yes

Todo / next steps
- Sync with finance (Karen Liu) to confirm VAT and credit handling rules (action: @Maya schedule 1:1)
- Spike: implement CSV generator and run on 2 historical invoices to validate schema (action: @Diego)
- Create design mockups for allocation editor + export modal (Figma) (action: @Samir)
- Add product spec to confluence and link in ticket PROD-1423 (action: @Priya)

Notes to self
- Keep headers stable: changing CSV schema will be disruptive to customers. Introduce schema_version column early.
- For MVP, avoid custom column mapping — ship standard schema and gather feedback.
- Think about a separate "reconciliation" API for customers to call with exported file to validate totals.

References
- existing export endpoints: /v1/billing/exports (backend) — needs extension
- related tickets: PROD-1423 (export schema), PROD-1462 (allocation UI), SE-83 (SFTP infra)

End of doc
